bugs: Minor: the claim TTL (15 min, app/Models/Subscriber.php:15) is shorter than UniqueFor(3600). After 15 minutes of backlog the dispatcher reclaims the row, but ShouldBeUnique silently rejects the push, so 'Queued N subscribers' overcounts (app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:26-27). No duplicate CRM calls result.
antipatterns: app/Models/Subscriber.php:17 uses the legacy scopeNeedsCrmSync naming instead of the #[Scope] attribute available in Laravel 12+
app/Models/Subscriber.php:15 has a public const claim TTL that isn't coordinated with UniqueFor(3600) at app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:17
Two dedupe layers (DB claim plus cache unique lock) give some belt-and-braces redundancy
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the swallowed exception, a dispatcher that ignores crm_sync_queued_at, the 24h default mutex expiry on withoutOverlapping, and chunk() over a column it mutates (fixed with chunkById)
Atomic conditional UPDATE claim, combined with lazyById and a reusable needsCrmSync scope
Uses modern Laravel 13 queue attributes (Tries, Backoff, Timeout, UniqueFor, DeleteWhenMissingModels), all verified in vendor
Removes WithoutOverlapping, whose default releaseAfter=0 and never-expiring lock were burning tries; ShouldBeUnique covers it
failed() records crm_last_error; the stale claim re-queues after recovery (probe confirmed end-to-end recovery)
Strong tests: a real queue:work run that lands in failed_jobs, a stale-claim re-queue test, a database-queue uniqueness test, a schedule expiresAt test, and a 250-row chunk-boundary test
Deleted subscribers are discarded rather than spamming failed_jobs

bugs: WithoutOverlapping->dontRelease() (app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:29) silently deletes a job that hits a held overlap lock. The probe showed the subscriber left unsynced while crm_sync_queued_at stays claimed, so it is not re-dispatched for 60 minutes. This is mostly harmless because the lock holder is usually syncing the same subscriber, but it can lose a sync if that holder then fails.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:16-18 uses public $tries/$timeout properties and a backoff() method instead of the Laravel 13 queue attributes
The test 'retries with backoff and enough attempts to survive overlap releases' contradicts dontRelease() (there are no releases) and only asserts config values
The test mutates $job->tries = 1 and uses an Http::swap(new Factory) hack where Http::fakeSequence would do
The claim query is inlined in the command (app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:23-26) rather than a reusable model scope
Recovery within the 60-minute claim is slow (probe: still unsynced 2 minutes after recovery, synced by 20 minutes)
strengths: Fixes all four root causes at the source: rethrow plus failed(), an atomic DB claim with stale TTL and lazyById, withoutOverlapping(10), and chunkById
CLAIM_MINUTES carries a single constraint comment that is accurate: worst-case retries are about 14 minutes, under 60
Adds expireAfter(120) on the job overlap lock, so killed workers do not leave permanent locks
The fresh() synced guard makes duplicates idempotent
Test suite covers failed_jobs via a real worker, stale re-queue, schedule expiry and the chunk boundary, including leaving already-normalized rows untouched

v.rationale: All three suites pass (impl-1 13, impl-2 11, impl-3 14), and all fix #1 (rethrow plus failed()), #3 (an expiring withoutOverlapping mutex) and #4 (chunkById). They differ on #2 and on how idiomatic the code is. impl-1 fixes the duplicates at the source with an atomic conditional-update claim through a model scope, adds ShouldBeUnique as a backstop, removes the WithoutOverlapping middleware that was burning tries, and uses Laravel 13 queue attributes. Its tests are the strongest, including real-worker failed_jobs and database-queue uniqueness. Probes confirmed recovery after an outage and no duplicate jobs during a backlog. impl-3 also fixes the dispatcher at the source with an atomic claim, but uses older property/method job config, and dontRelease() can silently drop a job (confirmed by a probe). Its tests are weaker: one asserts config values under a name that contradicts the code, and one uses an Http::swap hack. impl-2 never touches the dispatcher. It still re-dispatches every unsynced row every minute, rewrites crm_sync_queued_at and misreports counts (probe confirmed), relying only on a cache unique lock. It also stacks a redundant WithoutOverlapping and a dead crm_sync_queued_at reset, though its attribute usage is modern. Ranking: impl-1 > impl-3 > impl-2.
